full_judgment: 8. On behalf of the petitioner Mr. Khandaker Mahabubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate, first submits that the judgment of the Court of Appeal below is not a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as the learned District Judge did not consider all the material facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence taken into consideration by the Election Tribunal. On perusal of the judgment pronounced by the Courts below it appears that the Election Tribunal rejected the evidence of the PWs as, in his opinion, there were contradictions in the deposition of some of the witnesses and recorded a finding that the present Opposite Party No. 1 (the election petitioner) failed to prove that the petitioner resorted to any corrupt and unfair practice in the election at the said two centres. The learned District Judge reversed the said finding of the Election Tribunal and held that the petitioner resorted to corrupt practice in the election held on 10.2.1988 at Gangaprashad Primary School Centre and Kadamtali Madrasha Centre. In arriving at the said finding he found that all the PWs including PWs 6 and 7 who were Assistant Presiding Officers of Gangaprashad Primary Centre and Kadamtali Madrasha Centre respectively categorically stated that there was disturbance in the 2 centres and the voters could not exercise their right of franchise and they were not allowed to enter into those centres. He further noticed that on the date of election the election petitioner made similar allegations in writing addressed to the Returning Officer per Ext. 2. He also noticed that the counter foil of the ballot papers did not contain official mark, seal, and signature and that the petitioner in his evidence as OPW 3 admitted in cross- examination that he engaged some boats on that date and he paid Tk. 40.00 for each vote. The learned District Judge also adverted to the statements of the different PWs which were considered by the Election Tribunal to be contradictions and then found that those were not contradictions. He also considered the evidence of OPWs. It is no doubt true that each and every item of evidence referred to in the judgment of the Election Tribunal was not separately dealt with by the learned District Judge, but it is manifest upon a reading of his judgment that all the relevant evidence have been substantially considered in reversing the finding of the Election Tribunal. I thus find no substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
